newsitem.title: GREECE: IRS ASSISTANT IN ATHENS TO HELP U.S. CITIZENS.
newsitem.headline: IRS ASSISTANT IN ATHENS TO HELP U.S. CITIZENS.

text.p: An Internal Revenue Service (IRS) tax assistant will visit Greece, from March 4 to 7, to provide help on taxation issues to United States citizens residing in Greece, the U.S. Embassy said in a statement.

The tax assistor will be available to answer tax questions at the U.S. Embassy daily from 06:30 to 10:00 and 11:00 to 13:00 GMT, except on Wednesday March 5, when the office will be closed for the public from 11:00 onwards.
The same Federal income tax requirements that apply for Americans residing in the U.S. are also valid for U.S. residents who live in Greece, the statement said.
Therefore, all U.S. citizens with incomes over $ 6,550, if single, or $ 12,600 if married, should file a return, it added.

IRS has advised that effective December 31, 1996 anyone filing for a U.S. Federal Tax return or a dependent on this return should have a U.S. Social Security number or an Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN).
